npcs.name: Wenna Ashby
npcs.idle: If you're going south, mind the barrows. Nothing good's come out of them yet.

npcs.name: Dunstan the Carter
npcs.idle: Wheels, axles, horses. Ask me about any of 'em. Don't ask me about the road south.

npcs.name: Ysolde Huntington
npcs.idle: Rhodri says the old stories are for children. Rhodri says a lot of things.

npcs.name: Coel the Huntsman
npcs.idle: Good hunting on the plain this year. Too good. Makes a man careless.

npcs.name: Watch-Commander Osfrid
npcs.idle: Every giant on this plain is walking north. I've counted. I stopped counting.

npcs.name: the Abbess of Amesbury
npcs.idle: We tended the graves of the Long Knives for forty years. Now the giants tend them, with spades.

npcs.name: Bryn the Ostler
npcs.idle: The wild herd's the pride of the Downs. Was.

npcs.name: Elin the Herbwife
npcs.idle: Stone sheep. Stone hares. Stone shepherd, near enough.

npcs.name: Sister Morwen
npcs.idle: The dead on this plain were murdered at a feast. They have reason to be restless.

npcs.name: Outrider Cadoc
npcs.idle: The Watch's picket. Furthest south anyone sane will stand.

quests.title: Under the Stones
quests.offer:
My husband Aled took work guarding a wagon for some 'surveyors' bound south. Good coin, he said - too good, I said. That was nine days ago.

Dunstan the [carter] saw them go. I'm not asking you to fight anyone. Just - will you [find Aled]? Find him and tell me what kind of fool I married.

topics.carter: Dunstan. By the stables. He sees everything that leaves Ludlow, and has an opinion on all of it.

quests.summary: Wenna Ashby's husband hired on to guard a wagon of 'surveyors' bound south, and hasn't come home.

steps.goal: Ask Dunstan the carter where the wagon went
steps.say: Surveyors my eye. Shovels, rope, picks and a strongbox with nothing in it - you don't carry an empty strongbox to fill with *surveys*. They went south past the [barrows], where the tomb raiders dig. Aled knew. He's not a stupid man; he's a poor one.

steps.goal: Find the wagon near the tomb raiders' diggings
steps.text: The wagon's on its side, the horses gone. Aled's tally-stick is jammed in the wheel-spokes, as if he wanted it found - and every barrow round about has been opened.

steps.goal: Make the diggers talk
steps.text: The last digger talks fast. 'The drover? He wouldn't open the king's barrow. Said it was a grave and that was that. Foreman Brannoc had him trussed and dragged off to the old stones - for the ritual, he said. Laughed when he said it.'

steps.goal: Go to the great stones
steps.text: The ring of stones looms over the plain. Torches - and Aled, bound to a fallen lintel, very much alive and very much shouting.

steps.goal: Free Aled Ashby
steps.text: Aled's ropes are cut. He picks up a digger's shovel and looks almost cheerful about it.

stages.name: Keep Aled alive while he gets free
stages.objective: Keep Aled alive while he gets free
stages.announce: Brannoc's crew come running from the barrows. 'The drover's loose! Get him!'
stages.thanks: Well. That could have gone worse. Mostly for me.

stages.name: Foreman Brannoc
stages.announce: A big man with a pick shoulders through the stones. 'That's my barrow-king's gold, drover. Mine.'

steps.goal: Speak with Aled at the stones
steps.say:
Wenna sent you? Of course she did. Listen - before we go. I took this off Brannoc. It's from the king's barrow. Old gold. It would feed us for two winters, and I'd never need to take work from men like him again.

I know what it is. I know where it came from. Tell me straight: do I [put it back], or do we [keep it]?

options.say: ...Yes. Yes, that's the answer I was waiting for someone to give me. Take it back to the barrow for me? I can't go near the place again. I'll go home to Wenna.
Then it's ours, and the dead can complain to me personally. Go on - tell Wenna I'm coming. I'll be the one walking funny under all this gold.

steps.goal: Return the torc to the barrow-king's grave in the eastern barrows
steps.text: You lay the torc back on the bones of a king nobody remembers. The barrow sighs - you'd swear it - and settles.

steps.goal: Tell Wenna Ashby
steps.say:
He's home. Covered in mud, smelling of a wet dog, and home. He told me about the gold - and that you made him put it back.

Good. I'd rather be poor with him than rich with a curse in the house.

steps.goal: Tell Wenna Ashby
steps.say:
He's home, and he brought a king's torc into my kitchen. I've hidden it in the flour.

Two winters, he says. We'll see what the barrows say about it. Thank you - whatever comes of it, you brought him back.

honest.text: Aled carved you this - he says every debt deserves its notch.

gold.text: Take something from the barrow too. Aled says if there's a curse, it may as well be spread thin.

quests.title: The White Horse
quests.offer:
My brother Rhodri's gone after the White Horse. The real one - the one the hill-figure was cut for, before Camelot had a name. A lord in Ludlow will pay its weight in silver for the hide.

Coel says the plain's full of giants this year and Rhodri went alone. I don't care about the silver. Will you [bring him back]? Coel can show you his [tracks].

topics.tracks: Coel's by the fire. He taught Rhodri to track. He's not happy about how that turned out.

quests.summary: Rhodri Huntington went alone onto the giants' plain to hunt the White Horse of Salisbury.

steps.goal: Ask Coel about Rhodri's tracks
steps.say: He set a snare line east of the old drovers' road, where the horse comes to drink. Ran it right through the giants' grazing. Said giants were slow. Giants are slow - right up until they [aren't].

steps.goal: Find Rhodri's snare line on the giants' plain

clue.name: a snapped snare and a broken spear

steps.text: The snare's snapped and the spear's in three pieces. Huge prints all round - and a smear of blood leading east.

steps.goal: Drive off the giants who took him
steps.text: In the last giant's sack: Rhodri's quiver, empty. Whatever happened to him, he got away. The trail runs east to the old Roman bridge.

steps.goal: Follow the trail to the old Roman bridge
steps.text: Rhodri's under the bridge arch, white to the knees - grey, rather. A basilisk's glance, half-caught. He's alive, and very cross about it.

steps.goal: Kill the basilisk that hunts him
steps.text: The old basilisk sags and its eyes cloud over. The grey creeping up Rhodri's legs stops, and slowly starts to fade.

stages.name: the Old Gazer
stages.announce: Something heavy drags itself out of the reeds, and Rhodri swears. 'It followed me. Don't look at its eyes. Don't LOOK at its EYES.'

steps.goal: Talk to Rhodri
steps.say:
Ysolde sent you, didn't she. Of course.

I saw it, you know. The White Horse. Just before the giants came. It stood there looking at me like it knew my name. I could still have it - it drinks at the giants' pools at dusk. Help me, and the silver's half yours.

Or tell me to [let it be], and I'll limp home and listen to my sister laugh. Or we [hunt it] - now.

options.say: ...Yes. All right. I couldn't have loosed anyway, I think. Not with it looking at me. Let's go home.
Ha! Knew you had the stomach for it. Dusk, by the pools. Don't miss.

steps.goal: Hunt the White Horse at dusk
steps.text: It doesn't run. It only looks at you, and then it's down, and the light on the plain goes strange and flat. Far off on the hill, a crack runs through the chalk.

steps.goal: Return to Ysolde
steps.say:
He limped in with grey feet and a face like a wet week, and he said he saw it. The White Horse. And let it go.

You've no idea what that means to this family. Our grandmother used to say we keep the plain, not the other way round.

steps.goal: Return to Ysolde
steps.say:
The hill-figure cracked last night. Everyone in the camp heard it.

Rhodri's got his silver. He sits by the fire with it and doesn't say much. Take your share. I don't want it in my tent.

spared.text: Grandmother's horn. She'd want it to go to someone who listened.

quests.title: The Wild Herd
quests.offer:
The wild herd's run on these downs since before Camelot. Now the Downs Riders are cutting out the best and driving them north to sell.

Their camp's up by the river in the north. Will you [stop the riders]?
quests.summary: Bandits are driving off the Downs' wild herd from their camp in the north.

steps.goal: Fight off the Downs Riders on the horse-road about 130 m east of Bryn the Ostler
Defeat the Riders' leader at their camp
steps.text: The bandit leader falls. Behind the camp, a pen of frightened horses - and a bill of sale, to 'the man with the Cornish tin'.

steps.goal: Tell Bryn
steps.say:
Cornish tin? For horses? Who in Cornwall needs that many horses...

Never mind. The herd's free. Thank you.

quests.title: Stone-Eyed
quests.offer:
Stone sheep. I'm not jesting - grey stone, all the way through, standing in the grass with their mouths still chewing. The basilisks have come up from the south.

Will you [hunt the basilisks]? And bring me back an eye. Shut, mind.
quests.summary: Basilisks from the south are turning the Downs' flocks to stone.

steps.goal: Hunt the pseudo basilisks on the middle plain about 380 m south of Elin the Herbwife
Search the basilisk nest in the north-east
steps.text: The nest is ringed with stone things - a fox, a hare, a crow mid-flight. And eggs, warm. The basilisks didn't come up the plain. Something drove them.

steps.goal: Tell Elin
steps.say:
Drove them? Basilisks don't flee from much.

Unless what's coming is bigger than they are.

quests.title: Carrion on the Wind
quests.offer:
Carrion drakes on the north-west heath - more every week, and one big brute they call Slythcur. They follow the giants, my outriders say. Where giants walk, things die, and the drakes eat well.

Thin them, will you? [Clear the heath].
quests.summary: Carrion drakes gather on the north-west heath, following the giants' march.

steps.goal: Thin the carrion drakes on the heath about 480 m west of Watch-Commander Osfrid
Kill Slythcur
Report to Watch-Commander Osfrid
steps.say: Good. Now they'll have to follow the giants a bit hungrier.

quests.title: The Grove Nymphs' Bargain
quests.offer:
The grove nymphs of the middle plain never bothered anyone. This year they're striking at travellers. A woman called Veviel leads them.

The nymphs remember the plain before the stones. Will you [speak with Veviel]? By whatever means she'll allow.
quests.summary: The grove nymphs of the middle plain have turned hostile. The Abbess wants to know why.

steps.goal: Get past the grove nymphs about 460 m south of the Abbess of Amesbury
Face Veviel
steps.text: Veviel sinks into the grass. 'The ground shakes,' she whispers. 'The old ones are coming home to their stones. We only wanted them to pass us by.'

steps.goal: Tell the Abbess what Veviel said
steps.say:
'The old ones are coming home to their stones.' The giants. The nymphs are frightened, as we all are.

Shall I [send them word] that Amesbury will shelter their grove? Or [let them be]? Fear makes poor neighbours either way.

options.say: Then Sister Morwen will take them bread and willow-water. Frightened things can be friends.
Then we'll go round their grove, and they'll go round us.

quests.title: Spades on the Plain
quests.offer:
Tomb-raiders in the western fields - dozens, with spades and carts. They're opening the barrows one by one. Those are the graves of the Long Knives, and the Abbess is beside herself.

Will you [break the diggers]? And find out who's paying them.
quests.summary: Tomb-raiders are opening the barrows in the western fields.

steps.goal: Drive off the diggers in the western fields about 810 m south of Watch-Commander Osfrid
Search the diggers' camp
steps.text: Gold torcs, a broken crown, finger-bones still wearing rings. And a pay-chit: 'Forty ingots of Cornish tin, for every barrow opened to the bottom. Bring the bones to the stones.'

steps.goal: Show Osfrid the pay-chit
steps.say:
Cornish tin, paid by the barrow. 'Bring the bones to the stones.'

That's not grave-robbing. Robbers keep the gold. Somebody wants the dead moved.

quests.title: What the Spade Woke
quests.offer:
Under these barrows lie four hundred and sixty lords of Britain. Hengist the Saxon invited them to a peace-feast here, on the plain, and at a word his men drew knives and murdered them all. Merlin raised the Giants' Dance over their graves.

The diggers have woken them. Green ghasts walk the western fields, and a man called Cynewulf - a Saxon, a 'ghostwalker' - walks with them. Will you [lay them down]?
quests.summary: The diggers have woken the murdered lords of the Long Knives. A Saxon ghostwalker leads the ghasts.

steps.goal: Lay the green ghasts in the western fields to rest about 1.0 km south of the Abbess of Amesbury
Stop Cynewulf the Ghostwalker
steps.text: Cynewulf falls. 'My grandfather's grandfather held a knife at that feast,' he says. 'I came to say sorry. They didn't want to hear it.'

steps.goal: Tell the Abbess
steps.say:
He came to apologise. Four hundred years too late, and to the wrong people.

The ghasts are down. But the graves are open, and the dead won't stay down while they are.

quests.title: The Raiders' Paymaster
quests.offer:
The diggers in the west are only labour. The raiders on the eastern ridge are the ones who carry the tin. Their scouts watch every road.

Will you [follow the tin]? Fight through the scouts, break the eastern camp, and bring me their ledger.
quests.summary: The tomb-raiders' camp on the eastern ridge carries the Cornish tin that pays the diggers.

steps.goal: Fight through the tomb-raider scouts about 500 m south of Watch-Commander Osfrid
Break the raiders' camp on the eastern ridge
Search the raiders' camp for the ledger
steps.text: The ledger, in a careful hand: 'Received of Bolster, herald of the Wrath of Golestandt: tin, 900 ingots. Delivered to the stones: the bones of 212 lords. Remaining: 248. The dragon is patient. The giants are not.'

steps.goal: Bring the ledger to Osfrid
steps.say:
Golestandt. The dragon of Dartmoor - awake? I'd hoped that was a nursery tale.

He wants the dead out from under the stones. Two hundred and forty-eight left. We'd better be quick.

quests.title: The Night of the Long Knives
quests.offer:
The dead of the feast are walking the fields by night - not the ghasts the diggers woke. The old ones. Lords, still in their feast-clothes, looking for the men who killed them.

The Abbess says they must be told it's over. That Hengist is long dead and his sons with him. Will you [tell the dead]? They may not listen.
quests.summary: The murdered lords of the Long Knives walk the plain at night. Sister Morwen wants them told the war is over.

steps.goal: Calm the disturbed dead on the field of the feast about 180 m south-west of Sister Morwen
Search the old feasting-ground
steps.text: Under the turf, the stones of a long table. At its head, a cup - and in the cup, a ring with a red dragon on it.

steps.goal: Face the shade that rises at the table's head
steps.text: The Saxon shade breaks apart, and the field goes still. For the first time in four hundred years, nobody is waiting for the feast to end.

stages.name: the Shade of Hengist
stages.objective: Face the shade that rises at the table's head
stages.announce: A tall shade in Saxon mail stands up at the head of the table. 'Nimed eure saxes!' it roars - draw your knives - and the dead rise round you.

steps.goal: Tell Sister Morwen
steps.say:
Hengist's shade. Still giving the word, after all this time.

The ring - Ambrosius's, the Abbess will say. Do we [bury the ring] with the lords, so they know they were avenged? Or do you [carry it] for them, to the stones?

options.say: Then it goes back in the ground, and the lords rest. Bless you.
Then carry it well. The stones will know it.

quests.title: Wind Over the Barrows
quests.offer:
Wind mephits - little storm-devils - pour over the south-west downs and scour the barrows bare. The giants called them, the Abbess thinks: to blow the turf off the graves.

Will you [still the wind]? Kill enough and the rest lose heart.
quests.summary: Wind mephits are scouring the turf off the south-west barrows.

steps.goal: Kill the wind mephits on the south-west downs about 460 m south-west of Outrider Cadoc
Tell Outrider Cadoc
steps.say: Quieter already. I can hear myself think. Mostly I'm thinking about giants.

quests.title: Footprints Like Ponds
quests.offer:
Giants. Salisbury's own we've always had - big, slow, keep to the south. These are different. They walk in lines, north, and they carry stones.

Will you [scout their camps]? Kill a few if you must. I want to know where they came from.
quests.summary: Lines of giants are marching north across the plain, carrying stones.

steps.goal: Thin the giants on the southern plain about 440 m south of Outrider Cadoc
Search a giants' camp
steps.text: Bones of whole oxen. And stacked by the fire, blocks of grey granite flecked with pink - Dartmoor granite, from three hundred miles south, carried here on their backs.

steps.goal: Tell Outrider Cadoc
steps.say:
Dartmoor. They walked here from Dartmoor, carrying stones. To build what?

...To mend the Dance. Or to take it home.

quests.title: The Giants' Swine
quests.offer:
The giants drove herds of huge boars up with them - their larder on the hoof. The swine are rooting up every field from here to the river.

Cut down the herd and the giants go hungry. Hungry giants are slower. Will you [hunt the herd]?
quests.summary: The giants' herds of huge boars are rooting up the south downs.

steps.goal: Hunt the giants' huge boars about 610 m east of Coel the Huntsman
Tell Coel
steps.say: That's a winter's bacon for the whole village. And a few hungry giants. I'll take that trade.

quests.title: The Men Who Ran South
quests.offer:
Bandits in the far south - desperate ones, who fight like cornered dogs. Escaped, the locals say. From what, nobody knows.

Will you [find out]? Don't expect them to talk.
quests.summary: Escaped bandits in the far south fight like cornered dogs. Nobody knows what they escaped from.

steps.goal: Fight through the escaped bandits about 770 m south of Outrider Cadoc
Defeat the escaped bandits' leader
Search their camp
steps.text: Manacles - giant-sized, cut down with a file. A scratched note: 'Cottrel sold us to the stone-men. We dug round the stones' feet till our hands bled. Never again.'

steps.goal: Tell Outrider Cadoc
steps.say:
Cottrel. The slave master in the north-east. He's selling men to the giants as diggers.

The Commander will want to hear this.

quests.title: Slave Master Cottrel
quests.offer:
Cottrel keeps pens in the far north-east, and he's been selling men to the giants to dig round the Dance. Every one of them was somebody's son.

Will you [close the pens]? Bring friends. Cottrel's company are no farm-boys.
quests.summary: Slave Master Cottrel sells captives to the giants as diggers from his pens in the far north-east.

steps.goal: Break Cottrel's company about 750 m east of Watch-Commander Osfrid
Defeat Slave Master Cottrel
steps.text: Cottrel goes down among his own chains. 'The tin was good,' he says. 'Better than Camelot's silver.'

steps.goal: Tell Watch-Commander Osfrid
steps.say:
The pens are open? Good. There are eleven men in them, the outriders say.

We can [send them to Amesbury] - the Sisters will mend them. Or [send them to Camelot], to tell the Round Table what's on this plain. Witnesses are worth an army.

options.say: Then the Abbess will have them. She's good with broken things.
Then Camelot will hear it from men with giant-sized scars. They'll listen.

quests.title: The Giants' Dance
quests.offer:
The giants hold the Dance itself now - granite giants out of Dartmoor, bigger than anything Salisbury ever grew. The Abbess says Merlin bound the stones with a mark on the heel stone.

Will you [go to the Dance]? See the mark. Don't stay to fight what you can't.
quests.summary: Granite giants from Dartmoor hold the Giants' Dance. Merlin's binding mark is on the heel stone.

steps.goal: Reach the Giants' Dance about 690 m south of Watch-Commander Osfrid
steps.text: The stones rise over you, and giants walk between them like men among chairs.

steps.goal: Cut down the giants at the outer ring
Find Merlin's mark on the heel stone

clue.name: a stone with a mark worn almost smooth

steps.text: A star in a ring, worn nearly smooth - and scored across it, fresh, two marks: a claw like a dragon's, and a key under a crown, in red. Both of them want the stones.

steps.goal: Tell Osfrid
steps.say:
A key under a crown. The Crimson - Morgana's - here too? The dragon wants his giants' stones back, and Morgana wants Merlin's ring for something of her own.

And we're in the middle.

quests.title: The Giants' Dead
quests.offer:
The great barrow in the south-east isn't a lord's grave. It's older than the feast - older than Merlin. The giants who first raised the stones are buried there, and the raiders have opened it to the bottom.

What comes out of a giant's grave? Will you [go and see]? Take friends. Take many.
quests.summary: Tomb-raiders have opened the great barrow in the south-east - the grave of the giants who first raised the stones.

steps.goal: Fight through the mercenary tomb-raiders at the dig about 1.2 km south-east of the Abbess of Amesbury
Put down the giant skeletons risen from the barrow
Defeat Berik Liglim, master of the dig
steps.text: Berik Liglim falls by the barrow mouth. Below, in the dark, something enormous turns over in its sleep.

steps.goal: Tell the Abbess
steps.say:
Something enormous. Yes. The Sisters have a name for what sleeps under the great barrow: Gogmagog, the last giant of Albion, that Corineus threw into the sea at Cornwall. They brought his bones home.

God keep him sleeping.

quests.title: The Stone-Caller
quests.offer:
The giants' oracle - the stone-caller - stands at the heart of the Dance and sings to the stones. Every night they lean a little further toward the south. When they fall, the giants will carry them home, and Merlin's binding with them.

You've done everything we asked. This is the last of it. Will you [silence the stone-caller]?

topics.queen: She smiles. 'A long time ago. It's not a thing I talk about. Ask Sir Bedwyr at Prydwen, if you must - he knew me then.'

quests.summary: The giants' stone-caller sings the Giants' Dance loose from Merlin's binding, to carry it south.

steps.goal: Go into the heart of the Dance about 730 m south of the Abbess of Amesbury
steps.text: The singing fills the ring. The stones are leaning.

steps.goal: Silence Clochfaen the Stone-Caller
steps.text: Clochfaen falls among the stones, and the singing stops. Very slowly, the leaning stones settle back.

stages.name: Clochfaen the Stone-Caller
stages.announce: A giant robed in lichen turns from the stones, still singing. 'Little bones. The Dragon remembers when these stones were ours. So do we.'

steps.goal: Search the stone-caller's place
steps.text: Giant-runes, and under them in plain Albion, as if for you: 'The White Dragon wakes in Dartmoor. Merlin's tower fell, and the red fought the white, and the white was beaten. Now the white remembers. The stones are his. Then the Sleeper.'

steps.goal: Bring the tablet to the Abbess
steps.say:
'Then the Sleeper.' He means Arthur, on Avalon. First the stones, then the king.

I was a queen once. I know what a dragon's patience costs. Shall I [send to Camelot] with this, so the Round Table makes ready? Or will you [keep the tablet] and carry the warning yourself, south?

options.say: Then Camelot will have it by the new moon. Thank you - for the dead, and for the living.
Then carry it into the marsh, toward Avalon. Someone there will need to read it.
